docs.title: 5.1 The profiles \(f_n\) of each type
docs.text:
diff_rot.shapes (line 111) defines the shape of each degree; \(f_n\) = diff_rot_ampl × \(a_n\) × shape, with \(a_n\) = diff_rot_term_amp[n/2] (1 in the table below). With \(a\) = diff_rot_ampl, \(p\) = diff_rot_param, and \(x\) the fractional solar radius (diff_rot.solar_x: \(x = r\cdot\)r_out with a solar structure (background.md), \(x = r\) otherwise):

diff_rot_type \(f_0/a\) \(f_2/a\) \(f_n/a\), \(n \ge 4\) 'rigid' 1 'Y20' 1 'Y20-wall-bounded' \((1 - r)(r - r_i)\), \(r_i\) = ricb 'shellular' \(r^p - 1\) 'shellular_boussinesq' \(\tfrac12(1 - r^2)\) 'cylindrical' (\(a\varpi^2\)) \(\tfrac{2}{3}r^2\) \(-\tfrac{2}{3}r^2\) 'conical' (\(a\sin^2\theta\)) \(\tfrac{2}{3}\) \(-\tfrac{2}{3}\) 'solar' \((-7.695/435)\thinspace H(x)\) \((-86.04/435)\thinspace H(x)\) 'solar_P4' \((\Omega_{RZ} + (O_0 - \Omega_{RZ})E)/\Omega_{\rm ref} - 1\) \(O_2 E/\Omega_{\rm ref}\) \(O_4 E/\Omega_{\rm ref}\) (\(n = 4\)) 'tabulated' fit fit fit, up to diff_rot_nmax 'user' diff_rot_profiles[0] diff_rot_profiles[2] diff_rot_profiles[n]

Here \(H(x) = \tfrac12\left[1 + \tanh(2(x - 0.71)/0.1)\right]\) (the 'solar' frame is 435 nHz), and for 'solar_P4' \(E(x) = \tfrac12\left[1 + \mathrm{erf}((x - r_{tc})/d_{tc})\right]\) and \(\Omega_{CZ} = c_0 + c_2\cos^2\theta + c_4\cos^4\theta\) projected on Legendre polynomials (\(\cos^2\theta = (1 + 2P_2)/3\), \(\cos^4\theta = 1/5 + 4P_2/7 + 8P_4/35\)): \(O_0 = c_0 + c_2/3 + c_4/5\), \(O_2 = 2c_2/3 + 4c_4/7\), \(O_4 = 8c_4/35\).

'user'. diff_rot_profiles maps each even degree to a string, a numpy expression of r (kore radius), x (fractional solar radius) and p (diff_rot_param), evaluated in a namespace with only sin, cos, tan, arcsin, arccos, arctan, sinh, cosh, tanh, exp, log, log10, sqrt, abs, sign, pi, where, minimum, maximum, erf, erfc (no builtins). For example a cylindrical rotation:

par.diff_rot = 1; par.diff_rot_type = 'user'
par.diff_rot_profiles = {0: '(2/3)*r**2', 2: '-(2/3)*r**2'}
par.diff_rot_ampl = -0.25

builds matrices bitwise identical to diff_rot_type = 'cylindrical' with the same amplitude. The degrees must be even integers, and the strings must not contain #: spin_doctor.py ends each params.dat row of a 'user' run with them, after a # (diff_rot.description), so that every row carries its profile and np.loadtxt still reads the numeric columns.

'tabulated' (diff_rot._tabulated_fits, line 43). The file holds ome[θ, r] (nHz), r (R☉) and theta (rad). At each table radius, \(\Omega/\Omega_{\rm ref} - 1\) is interpolated in \(\cos\theta\) by a cubic spline and projected on \(P_n\) with 64 Gauss–Legendre nodes, \(f_n = \tfrac{2n+1}{2}\int(\Omega/\Omega_{\rm ref} - 1)P_n\thinspace dx\). Each \(f_n(r)\) is then fitted by least squares with a Chebyshev series:

  • by default (diff_rot_window = None with ricb > 0), on the table radii within 0.01 of the shell, of degree min(diff_rot_rdeg, half the number of radii);
  • with diff_rot_window = 'sun' (the default at ricb = 0), once over the whole Sun, of degree diff_rot_sun_deg, even in \(r\): the data are mirrored to \(-r\), continued below the first table radius by its value, and the odd coefficients are set to zero.

diff_rot_hold = \(x_h\), which held each \(f_n\) at \(f_n(x_h)\) below \(x_h\), was removed on 2026-10-26, and a run that sets it stops. It held every degree, so the latitudinal shear of the table at \(x_h\) filled the whole core. In bin/jsoc_hmi_2010_2026.npz that shear is about 4 nHz at 0.6 R☉, an artefact of the inversion; held from there, it gave the core spurious modes that mixed with the HFR modes. Its params.dat column stays, always nan.

The fit residuals and, for the shell fit, the truncation error of the expansion up to diff_rot_nmax are printed in nHz.

docs.title: 5.2 Derivatives and the full sphere
docs.text:
The operators need \(f_n\), \(r f_n'\) and \(r^2 f_n''\) on the Chebyshev nodes. diff_rot.fX (line 224) transforms the shape to \(N\) Chebyshev coefficients on the radial domain (utils.chebco_f, coefficients below \(10^{-14}\) of the largest dropped; cached per degree), evaluates the series or its derivatives (utils.funcheb) and multiplies by diff_rot_ampl and \(a_n\). So \(f'\) and \(f''\) are always consistent with the resolved \(f\), also for tabulated, step-like or 'user' profiles.

With ricb = 0 the radial coordinate is \(r \in [-1, 1]\) and each operator keeps only one parity of Chebyshev polynomials (§6.3). The shapes are therefore evaluated at \(\lvert r\rvert\), which makes \(f_n\) even, \(f_n'\) odd, and \(rf_n'\), \(r^2f_n''\) even. A shape with a kink at \(r = 0\) ('Y20-wall-bounded', 'shellular' unless \(p\) is even and positive, or a 'user' expression such as r) then converges slowly in \(N\); submatrices.py prints a WARNING for the predefined ones (line 245).

docs.title: 5.3 Profile codes
docs.text:
Each profile used in an operator has a three-letter code: two letters and the degree character diff_rot.DIGITS[n] (0–9, then a–z for 10–35):

code profile function (diff_rot.profile_functions) zf0, zf2, … \(f_n\) (zonal flow) fX(n, r, Dorder) zd0, zd2, … \(r f_n'\) Chebyshev fit of \(r\thinspace\)fX(n, r, 1) zs0, zs2, … \(r^2 f_n''\) Chebyshev fit of \(r^2\thinspace\)fX(n, r, 2) tw2, tw4, … \(p_0\sigma_n\) Chebyshev fit of \(p_0\thinspace\)sigmaX(n, r, 0) tp2, tp4, … \(p_0\sigma_n'\) (odd in \(r\), in utils.odd_profiles) Chebyshev fit of \(p_0\thinspace\)sigmaX(n, r, 1)

They are not in radial_profiles.proffdir until burrito first meets one and adds diff_rot.profile_functions(). With adiab_tw (ThermaD = 0 with the thermal wind) the tw, tp profiles are \(\sigma_n\), \(\sigma_n'\) without \(p_0\) (diff_rot._ptw), because those heat rows are divided by \(p_0\) (§7.2). A separate tp code is needed: a label such as h1tw21_D0 would mean \(r(p_0\sigma_2)'P\), the derivative of the product, not \(r p_0\sigma_2' P\).

docs.title: 5.4 The thermal-wind coefficients \(\sigma_n\)
docs.text:
diff_rot.sigma_coefficients(r) (line 251) solves (2.9) in Legendre space at all the radii at once, with the \(m = 0\) matrices of angular.py (the Schmidt harmonics of order 0 are the Legendre polynomials):

  • the Legendre coefficients of \(\Delta\Omega\) and \(\partial_r\Delta\Omega\) are the \(f_n\) and \(f_n'\) (fX); a product of two series is \(\sum_n f_n\thinspace P_n(X)\) applied to the other one, so \(F = 2\Delta\Omega + \Delta\Omega^2\) and \(\partial_r F = 2(1 + \Delta\Omega)\partial_r\Delta\Omega\) (thermal_wind = 2), or \(2\Delta\Omega\), \(2\partial_r\Delta\Omega\) (1);
  • multiplication by \(x\) is \(X\) and \((1 - x^2)\thinspace d/dx\) is \(D\), so the bracket of (2.9) is \(X\thinspace\partial_rF + DF/r\), and \((1 - x^2)\thinspace\partial_x S_{tw} = -\tfrac{r^2G^2}{\mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g}(I - X^2)(X\partial_rF + DF/r)\);
  • that is \(D\sigma\), which is solved for \(\sigma\) (with \(\sigma_0 = 0\), the \(l = 0\) part belonging to \(S_0\)) by forward substitution of \(h_k = (k+2)q_{k+1}\sigma_{k+1} - (k-1)p_{k-1}\sigma_{k-1}\) (_solve_D).

This is exact (no quadrature), for any degrees of \(\Delta\Omega\), and matches the closed forms (2.10) to \(2\times 10^{-16}\) of the natural scale \(r^2G^2\lvert\partial\Delta\Omega\rvert/(\mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g)\) (§9). The result is multiplied by thermal_wind_amplitude; thermal_wind = 3 gives \(\sigma_2 = -\tfrac23\)dSdtheta. sigmaX differentiates the Chebyshev series of \(\sigma_n(r)\) for \(\sigma_n'\). At ricb = 0, \(\sigma_n\) is even (\(f\) even, \(f'\) and \(g\) odd) and \(\sigma_n'\) odd, hence tp in odd_profiles.

docs.title: 6.1 Label grammar
docs.text:
A label names one radial operator: sX[fu1D1][fu2D2]_DY (utils.decode_label, line 68).

  • s: the section, u, v or h.
  • X: lowers the row's power of \(r\): the operator carries \(r^{p - X}\), with \(p\) = rpower_u (5) in u, rpower_v (3) in v, and 2 in h (1 when ThermaD = 0 without adiab_tw). Sections u and v also carry \(\rho_0\) to the power rhopower_u, rhopower_v (1 by default), section h no \(\rho_0\).
  • fu1D1, fu2D2: up to two profiles (§5.3) and their derivative orders. lho1, lho2 are \(h'\) and \(h''\).
  • _DY: the radial derivative order applied to the unknown.

For example, with the defaults, u2zd20lho1_D0 is \(r^3\rho_0\thinspace (r f_2')\thinspace h'\) acting on \(P\), and h1tw20lho1_D0 is \(r\thinspace p_0\sigma_2\thinspace h'\) acting on \(P\). rap.burrito evaluates \(r^{\rm rpower}\rho_0^{\rm rhopower} f_1 f_2\) on the Chebyshev nodes, utils.chebco_f transforms it, and utils.Mlam builds the multiplication matrix in the Gegenbauer basis \(C^{(\lambda)}\) of the section; submatrices.py then multiplies on the right by the derivative matrix and changes the basis: u is \(C^{(4)}\), v \(C^{(2)}\), h \(C^{(2)}\) (\(C^{(0)}\) if ThermaD = 0, \(C^{(1)}\) with adiab_tw). The diff-rot labels need at most \(P''\) in u, \(P'\) in v and \(P'\) in h, so they fit those bases. An operator that several terms share is computed only once.

docs.title: 6.2 The labels
docs.text:
diff_rot.labels() (line 443) lists every radial operator of the terms, and submatrices.py (line 191) adds them with the vector parity of their column (vP for \(P\) and \(s\), vT for \(T\)), after diff_rot.check():

  • for each degree \(n\) of \(\Delta\Omega\), the 18 momentum labels of the table of §3.4 (diff_rot.MOMENTUM with the codes of \(n\));
  • with thermal = 1 (_heat_labels, line 429): (a) h0pss0zf{n}0_D0 (\(r^2 p_0 f_n\); h0zf{n}0_D0 without pss if ThermaD = 0) for each degree of \(\Delta\Omega\); and for each degree \(n\) of \(S_{tw}\): (b) h1tp{n}0_D0 (\(r p_0\sigma_n'\), only if thermal_wind_radial = 1), (c) h2tw{n}0_D0, h1tw{n}0_D1, h1tw{n}0lho1_D0 (\(p_0\sigma_n\) times \(P\), \(rP'\), \(rh'P\)), (c′) h1tw{n}0_D0 (\(r p_0\sigma_n\) acting on \(T\), parity vT).

Like every other operator, each diff-rot matrix has its last chop rows dropped and that many zero rows added at the top, to make room for the boundary-condition rows of its row block, so the boundary conditions are unchanged by the differential rotation.

docs.title: 6.3 Parity in a full sphere
docs.text: At ricb = 0 the vector parity of the unknowns is \(v_P = (-1)^m\)symm for \(P\) and \(s\), and \(v_T = -v_P\) for \(T\). An operator has the parity \((-1)^{\text{rpower} + \text{dorder}_ 1 + \text{dorder}_ 2 + \text{DY} + \text{adj}}\), with adj = 1 for a first profile in utils.odd_profiles. utils.remroco keeps the rows of parity \(v\times\)(operator parity) and the columns of parity \(v\). This is correct only if every profile has the parity assumed: \(f_n\), \(rf_n'\), \(r^2f_n''\), \(\sigma_n\) even, \(\sigma_n'\) odd, \(h^{(k)}\) of parity \((-1)^k\); §5.2 explains how the profiles are made so. If a profile's Chebyshev coefficients of the wrong parity exceed \(10^{-8}\) of the largest, submatrices.py prints a WARNING: that part of the profile is dropped.

docs.title: 7.1 Momentum: diff_rot.momentum_block
docs.text:
operators.differential_rotation(l, section, component, offdiag) (line 113) calls diff_rot.momentum_block(l, section, component, offdiag, M) (line 470) with M the operators' namespace, where the .mtx matrices are loaded under their labels. For the row degree l (= \(l'\)), the section ('u' or 'v'), the column type ('upol' for \(P\), 'utor' for \(T\)) and offdiag = \(l - l'\), it sums over the degrees \(n\) of \(\Delta\Omega\) that couple this Δl (§3.5): \(\lvert\Delta l\rvert \le\) max_dl(n, …) and the parity of Δl; for each, the coefficient momentum_coef(name, n, l, m, offdiag) times the matrix of each label of momentum_labels(n, …). The result is multiplied by Gaspard and divided by \(L'^3\). Since each stored coefficient carries a factor \(L'\), the block is

\[ \frac{G}{L'^3}\sum(L'\times\text{coefficient})\times(\text{radial operator}) = \mathrm{row}(\mathbf W) \quad\text{of (3.6)} . \]

The \(1/L'^3\) makes these rows consistent with all the other momentum operators (§3.2). It returns [matrix, offd], offd the column block offset (utils.dr_offd, §7.3), or [0, 0] if no degree couples this Δl.

momentum_coefficients(n, m) (line 348) builds the coefficients once per \((n, m)\), for degrees up to lmax + n + 6 (building beyond lmax keeps the entries near lmax free of truncation errors), and stores them both as sparse matrices and by diagonal (angular.band, \(\lvert\Delta l\rvert \le n + 3\)), so that momentum_coef is an array lookup. The whole set takes milliseconds at lmax 1025.

docs.title: 7.2 Heat: diff_rot.heat_block
docs.text:
operators.thermal_diffrot (line 190) calls diff_rot.heat_block(l, component, offdiag, M) (line 489), which returns the section-h blocks of (3.9) times the row weight. With ThermaD > 0 the rows are \(r^2 p_0\times\)(eq)\(/L'^3\):

term component, \(\Delta l\) expression radial operator (a) 'temp', even, \(\lvert\Delta l\rvert \le n\) 1j*m*heat_coef('Pn')*M['h0pss0zf{n}0_D0'], times Gaspard \(i m G\thinspace r^2 p_0 f_n\thinspace s\) (b) 'upol', even, \(\le\) tw_nmax Ls*heat_coef('Pn')*M['h1tp{n}0_D0'] \(L_l\thinspace r p_0\sigma_n'\thinspace P\) (c) 'upol', even, \(\le\) tw_nmax heat_coef('dPnD')*(M['h2tw{n}0_D0'] + M['h1tw{n}0_D1'] + M['h1tw{n}0lho1_D0']) \(p_0\sigma_n(P + rP' + rh'P)\) (c′) 'utor', odd, \(<\) tw_nmax -1j*m*heat_coef('dPn')*M['h1tw{n}0_D0'] \(-i m\thinspace r p_0\sigma_n\thinspace T\)

with the sums over the degrees of \(\Delta\Omega\) for (a) and of \(S_{tw}\) for (b), (c), (c′). Ls is \(L_l\) of the source degree (from \(u_r = L_l P/r\)). The angular coefficients come from heat_coefficients(m) (line 383): \(X\), \(D\) from angular.Algebra up to lmax + max(8, \(n_{hi}\) + 4), and \(P_n(X)\), \(P_n'(X)\), \(P_n'(X)D\) for every even \(n\) up to the highest degree of \(\Delta\Omega\) and \(S_{tw}\), stored by diagonal. The column offset is the index difference in utils.ell.

Sign. The block is \(-\text{out}/L'^3\). The section-h rows of \(A\) hold the right-hand side of the heat equation (\(B\) = +entropy, thermal_advection = \(-r p_0 S_0' u_r\)), so the left-hand-side terms (2.11) enter \(A\) with a minus sign. In the momentum rows it is the opposite: \(B\) = −inertia, so the left-hand-side term \(\mathbf W\) enters \(A\) with a plus sign, as the Coriolis force does.

Factors of \(G\). (a) carries Gaspard explicitly; (b), (c), (c′) carry \(G^2\) through \(\sigma_n\), except with thermal_wind = 3.

Without thermal diffusion. With ThermaD = 0 the heat rows are divided by \(p_0\), which is about \(10^{-7}\) near the surface of a solar model and spoils the conditioning otherwise.

  • With thermal_wind = 0 the rows are \(r\times\)(eq)\(/p_0\) in \(C^{(0)}\), and (a) is h0zf{n}0_D0 (\(r f_n s\)).
  • With thermal_wind ≥ 1 (adiab_tw), (b) and (c) do not fit there: the weight \(r\) leaves \(P/r\) in (c), and \(C^{(0)}\) cannot hold \(P'\). The rows are then \(r^2\times\)(eq)\(/p_0\) in \(C^{(1)}\) (decode_label, line 90; submatrices.py, line 95), with the same labels, the tw, tp profiles without \(p_0\) (§5.3), and still no thermal boundary rows.

docs.title: 7.3 Assembly: assemble.py
docs.text:
assemble.py loops over the row degrees of each MPI rank. The unknown vector is [\(P\) blocks][\(T\) blocks][\(s\) blocks], each of N1 Chebyshev coefficients, with nb blocks per type. For row block \(l'\) (row row, diagonal column col0) and each Δl of diff_rot.dl_range(section, component) (line 457) whose source degree exists, it calls the operator and, unless it returned [0, 0], adds the block at column basecol + col0 + offd*N1:

rows column Δl (dl_range) lines u \(P\) (basecol = 0) \(-n_{\max}\) … \(n_{\max}\), step 2 262–270 u \(T\) (basecol = nb*N1) \(-n_{\max}-1\) … \(n_{\max}+1\), step 2 288–296 v \(P\) \(-n_{\max}-1\) … \(n_{\max}+1\), step 2 350–358 v \(T\) \(-n_{\max}\) … \(n_{\max}\), step 2 376–384 h \(s\) (basecol = 2*nb*N1), term (a) \(-n_{\max}\) … \(n_{\max}\), step 2 438–443 h \(P\), terms (b), (c) \(-n_{tw}\) … \(n_{tw}\), step 2 448–453 h \(T\), term (c′) \(1-n_{tw}\) … \(n_{tw}-1\), step 2 456–461

with \(n_{\max}\) the highest degree of \(\Delta\Omega\) and \(n_{tw}\) that of \(S_{tw}\). The momentum blocks are added with a plus sign to \(A\), whose momentum rows are Coriolis − viscous − buoyancy + diff rot; the heat blocks carry their sign already (§7.2). \(B\) is unchanged: the differential rotation has no time derivative. Forced runs (\(A - i\omega_f B\)) need no change either. \(A\) and \(B\) are then divided by \(\lVert A\rVert_F\) as usual.

The offset offd counts blocks, not degrees: the poloidal degrees of a symmetry class step by 2, so for a \(P\) (or \(s\)) column offd = \(\Delta l/2\); for a \(T\) column it is the index difference between the toroidal list and the poloidal one, which depends on the symmetry (utils.dr_offd, line 49).

docs.title: 8. Diagnostics
docs.text:
spin_doctor.py checks every solution against the energy, frequency and entropy budgets. With differential rotation, the terms couple different degrees, so a per-degree worker cannot evaluate them from its own degree alone. utils4pp.diff_rot_setup (line 569), called once per solution by utils4pp.diagnose, therefore:

  1. builds \(\mathbf u\) and \(\partial_r\mathbf u\) on the \((r_k, \cos heta)\) grid from the per-degree components (velocity), with lmax + 10 + max(\(n_{tw}\), \(n_{\max}\)) Gauss–Legendre nodes in \(\cos heta\). The harmonics \(Y_l\), \(\partial_ heta Y_l\) and \(Z_l\) come from angular.ylm_grid: the recurrence of \(X\) started at \(Y_m \propto \sin^m heta\), differentiated in \( heta\) for \(\partial_ heta Y_l\), and started at \(\sin^{m-1} heta\) for \(Y_l/\sin heta\), so that nothing is divided by \(\sin heta\). The recurrence is linear, so it is carried as a mantissa times a power of two per node: for large \(m\) the start \(\sin^{m-1} heta\) would underflow near the poles (from \(m \approx 330\) at \(l\) of a few thousand), and the mantissas are rescaled by \(2^{-600}\) when they grow past \(2^{600}\), which is exact. It is valid at any \(l\) and \(m\) (it matches exact rational values of \(P_l\) to \(\sim 10^{-13}\) up to \(l = 2000\), and keeps the norms to \(\sim 10^{-13}\) at \(m = 1425\), \(l = 3000\)), where scipy.special.sph_harm_y is NaN from \(l = 646\) on; utils.Ylm and utils.Ylm_full use it too;
  2. evaluates \(\Delta\Omega\), \(\partial_r\Delta\Omega\), \(\partial_r^2\Delta\Omega\), \(\partial_ heta\Delta\Omega\) there, as numpy Legendre series of the \(f_n\) (diff_rot.fX);
  3. forms the force \(\mathbf F = -\mathbf W\) of (2.6) and its radial derivative (the force closure, line 610), and projects them back on \((q, s, t)\) with (3.4): drforce[l];
  4. with thermal = 1, forms \(p_0[i m G\Delta\Omega s + \mathbf u\cdot abla S_{tw}]\) and projects it on \(Y_l\): drheat[l].

Only the profiles \(f_n\) come from diff_rot.py; the angular part here is independent of its algebra. The \(\sigma_n\) used here are computed by utils4pp.thermal_wind_entropy (line 489), which integrates (2.9) in \(x\) with numpy Legendre series at each radius and writes out its \(r\) derivative, not with diff_rot.sigma_coefficients. So the budgets test the assembled operators against a second implementation of the same equations.

The per-degree workers then add:

  • flow_worker (lines 761–769): Wdr = \(2 hinspace\mathrm{Re}\int ho_0\mathbf u^\ast\cdot\mathbf F hinspace dV\), Wdr_im its imaginary part, and Ensdr the enstrophy term \(( abla imes\mathbf u)\cdot( abla imes\mathbf F)\);
  • thermal_worker (lines 855–857): Wdr_thm = \(-2 hinspace\mathrm{Re}\int p_0 s^\ast[i m G\Delta\Omega s + \mathbf u\cdot abla S_{tw}] hinspace dV\).

spin_doctor (lines 389–395) includes them in the residuals:

\[ egin{aligned} ext{resid}\sigma &: \quad 2\sigma hinspace KE - D_{kin} - W_{thm} - W_{dr} = 0,\cr ext{resid}\omega &: \quad 2\omega hinspace KE + W_{cor,im} - D_{kin,im} - W_{thm,im} - W_{dr,im} = 0,\cr ext{resid}s &: \quad 2\sigma hinspace TE - D_{thm} - W_{adv} - W_{dr,thm} = 0 , \end{aligned} \]

and the enstrophy residual includes Ensdr. By §2.3, only the shear part of \(\mathbf W\) contributes to Wdr; the Doppler and local-Coriolis parts appear in Wdr_im. The diff-rot options are written to params.dat (spin_doctor.param_table: diff_rot_ampl, the \(a_n\), diff_rot_param, and diff_rot_type as its index in diff_rot.TYPES, with a 'user' run's profile definitions at the end of the row after #), and Wdr, Wdr_im, Ensdr, Wdr_thm to flow.dat and thermal.dat.

docs.title: 9. Internal consistency checks
docs.text:
These checks test the implementation against itself and against exact results, not against published calculations.

  • bin/ru_insane.py, after submatrices.py (no MPI, seconds; needs N ≥ 96). With diff_rot = 1, dr_blocks (line 200) packs the diff-rot blocks as assemble.py does, and the test pairs them with random smooth fields, comparing each \(P\)/\(T\) part against a direct \((r, \cos heta)\) quadrature of \(\int ho_0\mathbf x^\ast\cdot G[(\mathbf U_0'\cdot abla)\mathbf y + (\mathbf y\cdot abla)\mathbf U_0'] hinspace dV\); the heat blocks against \(-\int p_0 x_s^\ast hinspace i m G\Delta\Omega hinspace y_s\) (and their anti-Hermitian symmetry) and against \(-\int p_0 x_s^\ast hinspace \mathbf u(y)\cdot abla S_{tw}\); and for 'rigid', the block identities of §3.6: \(R = a(i m G I + C)\), (a) \(= -i m G a E\), thermal-wind blocks zero. A 1 % error in one coefficient of one \(\Delta l\) shows up at \(10^{-4}\) to 1. Its grid uses only the profiles of diff_rot.py: \(\Delta\Omega\) as numpy Legendre series, \(\partial_ heta S_{tw}\) pointwise from the balance, \(S_{tw}\) by Gauss integration in \(x\), \(\partial_r S_{tw}\) by Chebyshev differentiation.
  • tests/diff_rot/angular_check.py (standalone, 30 s; --quick 4 s): the harmonics of angular.ylm_grid against exact rational values of \(P_l\) (up to \(l = 2000\)), against scipy (\(l \le 640\)), and their norms up to \(l = 3000\); \(X\) and \(D\) applied on a grid, and \(X^\dagger = X\), \(D^\dagger = 2X - D\); every vector operation of §3.3 against grid projections of the same fields, at low degree and around \(l = 1200\); the primitives against the former quadrature builder (quad_reference.py, \(n\) up to 16). References evaluated on a grid have their own floor of about \(\epsilon l^2\) near the poles, so their tolerance is max(\(10^{-11}\), \(10^{-15}l^2\)).
  • tests/diff_rot/gen_check.py [mmax [nmax [lmax]]]: the couplings of diff_rot.py against the closed forms of tests/diff_rot/diff_rot_coefficients.py, relative to the largest coefficient of the same row block (\(\le 1.3 imes 10^{-15}\) at lmax 20 and 1025); the selection rules of §3.5 for \(n\) = 4 to 16 (the coefficients outside them are exactly zero); and for runs with \(P_0\), \(P_2\) only and thermal_wind 1 or 2, the \(\sigma_n\) of diff_rot.sigma_coefficients against (2.10) (\(\le 2 imes 10^{-16}\) of \(r^2G^2\lvert\partial\Delta\Omega vert/(\mathrm{Beyonce} hinspace g)\)).
  • tests/diff_rot/regress.sh OLD_KORE: \(A\) and \(B\) against an older checkout, bitwise or at round-off (\(< 10^{-13}\) of each row's scale), on 15 configurations (including 'solar_P4' and a 'user' profile with degrees 0, 2, 4). Each is written with both parameter namings (§4.1), and the one of the checkout is used.
  • tests/heat_dr/ (run_all.sh): tw_sympy.py (the closed forms (2.10) against (2.9)), heat_check.py (the heat operators against a grid quadrature, and the \(\sigma_n\) fits against an independent integration of (2.9), any degrees), rigid_thermal.py (the identity (2.12) with the heat equation), asm_check.py, row_check.py, ebal.py (budgets from the matrix rows), mpi_check.sh (bitwise on 1–4 ranks), and others.
  • spin_doctor residuals (§8), for every run: they close to round-off for a resolved mode, and are the check of resolution in \(N\) and lmax. With lmax ≥ 646 they were NaN before angular.ylm_grid replaced scipy's harmonics.

docs.title: 10. Limitations
docs.text:
• The profiles do not depend on the background model, except that solar_x takes \(x = r\cdot\)r_out with a solar structure (background.md).
  • The degree character of the profile codes limits the degrees to 35: \(n_{\max} \le 16\) with thermal_wind = 2 (\(S_{tw}\) up to \(2n_{\max} + 2 = 34\)), \(n_{\max} \le 32\) with thermal_wind = 1; diff_rot.check stops otherwise.
  • 'user' expressions are evaluated with Python's eval in a namespace without builtins: enough to stop accidents, not a sandbox for untrusted input.
  • The inviscid formulation (ViscosD = 0, rows times \(\rho_0^2\)) builds the same labels with different weights, but is untested with differential rotation, and ru_insane.py does not cover it.
  • With thermal_wind = 1 the eigenvalues depend on the choice of frame at second order in \(\Delta\Omega\); thermal_wind = 2 is frame independent.
  • The \(p_b S_0'\) term of the thermal wind is omitted (§1.4); it matters where \(S_0' \neq 0\), e.g. in a radiative interior (stratification 'solar_rz').
  • With ThermaD = 0 and the thermal wind, the boundary layer that a small ThermaD would form at fixed-entropy walls is absent, and small-scale growing modes peaking at \(l \approx\) lmax can appear that do not converge in lmax.
  • The matrices widen with the highest degree: the momentum rows couple \(n_{\max} + 1\) degrees on each side, the heat rows \(n_{tw}\) = \(2n_{\max} + 2\) with thermal_wind = 2. 'tabulated' with a large diff_rot_nmax is the most expensive case (§12). Sharp profiles (the 'solar' tachocline at ricb = 0) need large N (about 400).

docs.title: 11.1 Set-ups and conventions
docs.text:
kore. Fields go as \(\exp(\lambda t + im\phi)\) in the frame rotating at \(\Omega_{\rm ref}\), with \(\lambda = \sigma + i\omega\), \(\sigma < 0\) damped and \(\omega < 0\) prograde.

Baruteau & Rieutord 2013. Fields go as \(\exp(i\Omega_p t + im\phi)\) in the inertial frame. They quote \(\lvert\omega\rvert = \lvert\mathrm{Re}\,\Omega_p\rvert\) and \(\tau\) (\(< 0\) damped) in units of \(\Omega_{\rm ref}\), where \(\Omega_{\rm ref}\) is \(\Omega\) at the surface (shellular) or on the axis (cylindrical). - Conversion: \(\Omega_p = \omega - m\) and \(\tau = \sigma\). Their \(m = -6\) mode is kore's \(m = 6\) with \(\Omega_p \to -\overline{\Omega_p}\). - \(E = \nu/(\Omega_{\rm ref}R^2)\) = ViscosD. Stress-free walls, \(\eta = 0.35\) unless stated, equatorially symmetric modes (symm = 1) unless stated. - kore: diff_rot_type = 'shellular' with diff_rot_param \(= \sigma\) (ΔΩ \(= r^\sigma - 1\)), or 'cylindrical' with diff_rot_ampl \(= \varepsilon\) (ΔΩ \(= \varepsilon r^2\sin^2\theta\)). Uniform density (structure 'uniform'), thermal = 0.

Guenel et al. 2016. The same equations and conventions as Baruteau & Rieutord 2013 (their eqs. 4–6), with \(\Omega = 1 + \varepsilon\sin^2\theta\) in units of the pole rate \(\Omega_{\rm ref}\): kore's 'conical' with diff_rot_ampl \(= \varepsilon\), in the frame rotating at the pole. Their figure labels give \(\lvert\omega\rvert\) only. For \(m = 2\) the sign of \(\Omega_p\) is the one in their text (Figs. 14, 15) or the only one inside the inertial range \(\lvert\Omega_p + m\Omega(\theta)\rvert < 2\Omega(\theta)\) (Fig. 13).

Mirouh et al. 2016. Their equations (2.7)–(2.9) are kore's with: - structure 'uniform' and stratification 'linear': \(\rho = p_0 = 1\), \(g = r\), \(dS/dr = r\), so the advection term is \(r v_r\); - Beyonce \(= N^2\) and ThermaD \(= E/P\), with \(T = 0\) at both walls; - 'shellular_boussinesq' with diff_rot_ampl \(= N^2\), and thermal_wind = 0. Their background is balanced by centrifugal buoyancy, which kore does not carry.

They also use the inertial frame: \(\lambda = \tau + i\omega\), so \(\omega = \omega_{\rm kore} - m\) and \(\tau = \sigma\).

Solar papers. - Frequencies are in nHz in the frame rotating at 456 nHz, with negative values retrograde, followed by the growth rate. - Model S density, \(\nu = \kappa = 10^{12}\) cm² s⁻¹, adiabatic convection zone, stress-free walls (set-ups in docs/heat-equation.md §8 and §9). - "With thermal wind" means thermal_wind = 2 (the exact \(\Omega^2\)) without \(u_r\,\partial_r S_{tw}\) (thermal_wind_radial = 0). - 2025a: shell 0.71–0.985 R☉, N 64, lmax \(m + 63\). 2025b: rin 0.5 R☉, N 128.

docs.title: Differential rotation in the heat equation: derivation, implementation, benchmarks
docs.text:
kore has long included a differential rotation of the background in the momentum equation. This page explains why it must also enter the heat (entropy) equation, and records how that was derived, coded and tested. If you only want to run the code, start with the user guide, differential-rotation.md, which lists the parameters, profiles and examples. This page is the reference behind it.

The physics in two sentences. A perturbation is carried around by the mean flow, so its entropy is advected by the differential rotation. And a star whose rotation rate varies with latitude and depth is only in equilibrium if its entropy also varies with latitude (thermal-wind balance); the flow of a perturbation across that latitudinal entropy gradient changes its entropy, which feeds back on the motion through buoyancy.

How the page is organised:

  • Notation and code names defines the symbols and the kore jargon used below.
  • §0 states the result: three new terms in the heat equation.
  • §1 derives the background entropy \(S_{tw}\) that thermal-wind balance requires.
  • §2 writes the three terms in kore's spherical-harmonic form.
  • §3 explains how they map onto kore's matrices and operator labels.
  • §4 lists the published benchmarks and which terms each needs.
  • §5 records the implementation and its tests.
  • §6 compares with the solar inertial-mode calculations of Bekki et al. 2022 and Mukhopadhyay et al. 2025.
  • §7 lists what is still open.
  • §8 generalises the rotation profile to any Legendre degree ('solar_P4', 'tabulated') and repeats the solar benchmark like for like.
  • §9 adds the radiative interior of Mukhopadhyay et al. 2025b, fits of Model S and of a tabulated \(\Omega\) over the whole Sun, and follows the solar inertial modes as the inner boundary moves from 0.71 R☉ to the centre.

History. The terms were derived on 2026-10-11 and committed in three steps on anelastic_log:

  1. the heat-equation terms (be2a4db5);
  2. the Gaspard factors, the exact and prescribed thermal wind, ThermaD = 0 (with thermad0.md) and the spin_doctor diagnostics (18641206);
  3. any \(P_n\), 'solar_P4', 'tabulated' and the amplitude controls (92a0d020, §8).
  4. the radiative interior, the whole-Sun Model S and \(\Omega\) fits, and ricb = 0 for 'model S' (§9).

The checks are in tests/heat_dr/ and tests/diff_rot/.

§5 to §9 record what was run between 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-24, in the parameter names of that time. Since 2026-10-26 the background is chosen by structure, stratification and diffusivity instead (background.md translates the former names): 'user def' is structure 'Wu 2005' with stratification 'top hat'; 'smoothed sun' is a solar structure ('8-term fit' for solar_density = 'fit', 'old model S prototype' for 'model S') with stratification 'odd top hat' and diffusivity 'step', or both 'solar_rz' for solar_rz = 1; 'Boussinesq' is 'uniform'; and aux0 is r_out. The amplitude diff_rot_amplitude is diff_rot_ampl since 2026-10-23 (differential-rotation.md), and the code these sections describe (diff_rot_generic.py, heat_dr_coefficients.py and the differential-rotation parts of radial_profiles.py and utils.py) is now in bin/diff_rot.py and bin/angular.py (differential_rotation_details.md).

docs.title: Notation and code names
docs.text:
Everything is dimensionless, in kore units: the length unit \(R\) is the outer radius of the shell, and the time unit is \(1/\Omega_0\) unless stated otherwise (see Gaspard below).

symbol meaning name in the code \(r\), \(\theta\), \(\phi\) spherical coordinates; \(x = \cos\theta\) \(\Omega_0\), \(\Omega_{\rm ref}\) rotation rate of the frame in which kore solves diff_rot_frame (in nHz, solar profiles) \(G\) \(\Omega_{\rm ref}\tau\), the frame's rotation rate in kore's time unit \(\tau\) (the Coriolis factor); 1 with timescale = 'rotation' Gaspard \(\Delta\Omega(r, \theta)\) relative differential rotation: \(\Omega = \Omega_0\thinspace (1 + \Delta\Omega)\) chosen by diff_rot_type \(f_n(r)\) Legendre coefficients of \(\Delta\Omega\) in \(\cos\theta\) abu (\(f_0\)), aub (\(f_2\)), ab4, … \(\mathbf U_0\) the azimuthal mean flow of \(\Delta\Omega\), seen in the rotating frame \(s\) entropy perturbation, \(\delta s/c_p\) the unknown of section h \(S_0(r)\) background entropy (spherical part); \(S_0'\) its radial gradient dSd; pdS is \(p_0 S_0'\) \(S_{tw}(r, \theta)\) latitudinal background entropy required by thermal-wind balance (§1) \(\sigma_n(r)\) Legendre coefficients of \(S_{tw}\) in \(\cos\theta\) tw2 is \(p_0\sigma_2\), tp2 is \(p_0\sigma_2'\), … \(\rho_0\), \(T_0\), \(p_0\) background density, temperature, and \(p_0 = \rho_0 T_0\) pss is \(p_0\) \(h\) \(\ln\rho_0\) lho \(g(r)\) gravity profile gra Beyonce buoyancy scale: the buoyancy force is \(\mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g\thinspace s\thinspace \hat{\mathbf e}_ r\) Beyonce ThermaD, \(\kappa\) thermal diffusion number and diffusivity profile ThermaD; kps is \(\kappa p_0\) \(P\), \(T\) poloidal and toroidal scalars of the velocity \(\mathbf u\) sections u and v \(l\), \(m\), \(L\) harmonic degree, azimuthal order, \(L = l(l+1)\) l, m \(i\thinspace m\) the imaginary unit times \(m\): fields go as \(e^{i m\phi}\), so \(\partial_\phi \to i\thinspace m\) \(l'\), \(\Delta l\) target degree (matrix row) and \(\Delta l = l' - l\) offd \(S_l^m\) Schmidt-normalised spherical harmonics ut.Ylm

Code concepts used on this page:

  • Sections. kore stacks its unknowns in blocks: u (poloidal scalar \(P\), from the radial component of the curl of the curl of the momentum equation), v (toroidal scalar \(T\), from the radial component of the curl) and h (the entropy \(s\), from the heat equation). "Section h" means the matrix rows that hold the heat equation.
  • Eigenproblem. kore solves \(A\mathbf x = \lambda B\mathbf x\). The real part of \(\lambda\) is the growth rate, and the frequency is minus its imaginary part.
  • Row weights. Before projection each equation is multiplied by a power of \(r\) (and in section h by \(p_0\)), so that its radial coefficients are polynomials and the matrices are banded. Every operator is also divided by \(L^3\), a normalisation common to all of kore's operators.
  • Gegenbauer bases. The rows are projected on Gegenbauer polynomials \(C^{(k)}\) (gebasis in submatrices.py). A row with radial derivatives up to order \(k\) needs at least the \(C^{(k)}\) basis; section h uses \(C^{(2)}\) by default.
  • Operator labels. Each radial operator is named by a short string, read by utils.decode_label. For example h1tw20_D0 means: section h; 1 lowers the row's power of \(r\) by one; the profile tw2 with derivative order 0; and _D0, no radial derivative of the unknown. A second profile can follow the first (h1tw20lho1_D0 is \(r\thinspace p_0\sigma_2\thinspace h'\) acting on \(P\)).
  • Parity in a full sphere. With no inner core (ricb = 0) kore expands each radial function in Chebyshev polynomials of one parity in \(r\). Every profile must then be even or odd in \(r\), and the odd ones are listed in the adj lists of submatrices.py.
  • Symmetry. symm = ±1 selects the equatorial symmetry of the mode; it fixes which degrees \(l\) appear for each unknown (ut.ell).
  • LBR. The Lantz–Braginsky–Roberts form of the anelastic approximation, in which the buoyancy depends on the entropy perturbation only.

docs.title: 0. Result in brief
docs.text:
kore's heat equation is the set of rows of section h, built by operators.entropy, thermal_advection and thermal_diffusion:

\[ p_0 hinspace rac{\partial s}{\partial t} = -p_0 hinspace u_r S_0' + \mathrm{ThermaD} hinspace abla\cdot(\kappa hinspace p_0 abla s), \qquad p_0 = ho_0 T_0. \]

In words: the entropy perturbation changes because the radial flow carries fluid across the background entropy gradient, and it diffuses.

The rows are multiplied by \(r^2\). Without thermal diffusion (ThermaD = 0) they are also divided by \(p_0\), and the weight is \(r\) instead of \(r^2\) unless the thermal wind is on (§3 and thermad0.md).

Now let the background rotate differentially,

\[ \Omega = \Omega_0 hinspace [1 + \Delta\Omega(r, heta)], \qquad \Delta\Omega = f_0(r) + f_2(r) hinspace P_2(\cos heta). \]

(§0 to §7 use this \(P_0 + P_2\) form; §8 extends it to any even degree.) Two things change.

  • The perturbation is advected by the mean flow of the differential rotation,
\[ \mathbf U_0 = \Delta\Omega hinspace r\sin heta hinspace \hat{\mathbf e}_ \phi . \]
  • The background entropy acquires a latitudinal part \(S_{tw}(r, heta)\), fixed by thermal-wind balance (§1).

Linearising

\[ rac{\partial s}{\partial t} + \mathbf U_0\cdot abla s + \mathbf u\cdot abla(S_0 + S_{tw}) = ext{diffusion} \]

adds three terms to the left-hand side of the heat equation:

\[ p_0\left[ hinspace i hinspace m hinspace \Delta\Omega hinspace s + u_r hinspace rac{\partial S_{tw}}{\partial r} + rac{u_ heta}{r} hinspace rac{\partial S_{tw}}{\partial heta} ight]. \qquad (1) \]

They are, in order:

  • (a) advection. The perturbation is carried around at the local rotation rate. On its own this only shifts frequencies (it is the Doppler shift of a rigid rotation, made local).
  • (b) radial. The radial velocity moves fluid across the radial gradient of \(S_{tw}\).
  • (c) latitudinal. The meridional velocity moves fluid across the latitudinal gradient of \(S_{tw}\). This is the baroclinic coupling. In §2 it splits into (c), from \(P\), and (c′), from \(T\).

The first term follows from the linearisation alone. The other two come from the background entropy, which in kore's framework is the thermal wind of §1 (kore's background is spherical in \( ho_0\), \(T_0\) and \(g\), has no mean centrifugal term, and uses LBR buoyancy). Terms (b) and (c) must be switchable (thermal_wind), because the Boussinesq benchmark of Mirouh et al. 2016 imposes \(\Omega(r)\) with a purely radial \(T_0\) (§4).

Nothing else changes:

  • The momentum equation keeps its present diff-rot term. The background pressure is a gradient and drops out of the curled equations, and the buoyancy stays \(\mathrm{Beyonce} hinspace g hinspace s hinspace \hat{\mathbf e}_ r\).
  • The diffusion acts on \(s\) only: \(S_{tw}\) is assumed to be maintained, like \(S_0\).
  • The mean flow does not advect \(S_{tw}\), because \(S_{tw}\) does not depend on \(\phi\): \(\mathbf U_0\cdot abla S_{tw} = 0\).
  • There is no viscous heating in kore.

§2 gives the terms in kore's harmonic form, §3 what they need in the code.

docs.title: 1. Thermal-wind entropy S_tw
docs.text: A rotation rate that varies along the rotation axis cannot be balanced by pressure alone. The centrifugal and Coriolis forces of the differential rotation then have a curl, and in a stratified fluid only a buoyancy force that varies with latitude can balance it. This is thermal-wind balance. This section computes the latitudinal entropy \(S_{tw}\) that kore's background must therefore have, and estimates its size.

docs.title: The balance
docs.text:
Consider the steady background in the rotating frame, in kore units: time \(1/\Omega_0\), length \(R\), and buoyancy \(\mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g(r)\thinspace s\thinspace \hat{\mathbf e}_ r\), so that

\[ N^2 = \mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g\thinspace \frac{dS}{dr}. \]

The momentum balance of the mean flow is

\[ \mathbf U_0\cdot\nabla\mathbf U_0 + 2\hat{\mathbf z}\times\mathbf U_0 = -\nabla p_b + \mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g\thinspace S_{tw}\thinspace \hat{\mathbf e}_ r . \]

Its left side, the centrifugal and Coriolis forces of the differential rotation, is

\[ -\left[(1+\Delta\Omega)^2 - 1\right] r\sin\theta\thinspace \hat{\mathbf e}_ s , \]

where \(\hat{\mathbf e}_ s\) is the cylindrical radial unit vector. Taking the curl removes the pressure, and its \(\phi\)-component gives

\[ \frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial S_{tw}}{\partial\theta} = \frac{r\sin\theta}{\mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g(r)}\thinspace \frac{\partial (1+\Delta\Omega)^2}{\partial z} \qquad (2) \]

where \(z\) is the coordinate along the rotation axis:

\[ \frac{\partial}{\partial z} = \cos\theta\thinspace \frac{\partial}{\partial r} - \frac{\sin\theta}{r}\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta}. \]

Equation (2) is the thermal-wind equation in kore's variables. In dimensional form it reads

\[ r\sin\theta\thinspace \frac{\partial\Omega^2}{\partial z} = \frac{g}{c_p\thinspace r}\thinspace \frac{\partial S}{\partial\theta}, \]

which is eq. (27) of Bekki, Cameron & Gizon 2022 (A&A 662, A16). The \(l = 0\) part of \(S_{tw}\) is absorbed in \(S_0(r)\).

docs.title: Linear and exact forms
docs.text:
To first order in \(\Delta\Omega\), replace \((1+\Delta\Omega)^2\) by \(1 + 2\Delta\Omega\). Then (2) integrates in closed form:

\[ \begin{aligned} S_{tw} &= \sigma_2(r)\thinspace P_2(\cos\theta) + \sigma_4(r)\thinspace P_4(\cos\theta),\cr \sigma_2 &= -\frac{2r^2}{\mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g}\left[\frac{f_0'}{3} + \frac{f_2'}{21} + \frac{4}{7}\frac{f_2}{r}\right],\cr \sigma_4 &= -\frac{6r^2}{35\thinspace \mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g}\left[f_2' - \frac{2f_2}{r}\right]. \end{aligned} \qquad (3) \]

This linear form is thermal_wind = 1.

Keeping the \(\Delta\Omega^2\) term gives the exact form, thermal_wind = 2. It changes \(\sigma_2\) and \(\sigma_4\) by products of the profiles and adds a \(P_6\) component. In addition, when kore's time unit \(\tau\) is not \(1/\Omega_{\rm ref}\), so that \(G\) = Gaspard = \(\Omega_{\rm ref}\tau \neq 1\), the right side of (2) gets a factor \(G^2\). With \(e = 0\) for thermal_wind = 1 and \(e = 1\) for thermal_wind = 2, the closed forms are (checked by tests/heat_dr/tw_sympy.py):

\[ \begin{aligned} \sigma_2 &= -\frac{2r^2G^2}{\mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g}\left[(1+e f_0)\left(\frac{f_0'}{3} + \frac{f_2'}{21} + \frac{4}{7}\frac{f_2}{r}\right) + \frac{e\thinspace f_2\thinspace (f_0' + f_2')}{21}\right],\cr \sigma_4 &= -\frac{6r^2G^2}{35\thinspace \mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g}\left[(1+e f_0)\left(f_2' - \frac{2f_2}{r}\right) + e\left(f_2 f_0' + \frac{4}{11} f_2 f_2' + \frac{14}{11}\frac{f_2^2}{r}\right)\right],\cr \sigma_6 &= -e\thinspace \frac{4r^2G^2}{77\thinspace \mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g}\thinspace f_2\left(f_2' - \frac{2f_2}{r}\right). \end{aligned} \qquad (3') \]

How much the exact form matters. For the conical profile below, it multiplies \(\sigma_2\) by \(1 + 2\varepsilon/3\) and \(\sigma_4\) by \(1 + 12\varepsilon/11\): 17 % and 27 % for \(\varepsilon = -0.25\). The \(\sigma_6\) term needs

\[ P_6(X) = \frac{231X^6 - 315X^4 + 105X^2 - 5}{16} \]

and couplings \(\Delta l = \pm 6\) (for \(P\)) and \(\pm 5\) (for \(T\)) in §2 and §3.

Frame independence. Only the exact form is independent of the frame: a run in a frame rotating at \(\Omega_{\rm ref}(1 + c)\), with \(f_0\) shifted by \(-c\), gives the same modes. With the linear form the choice of frame moves the modes slightly (§6).

docs.title: Checks on simple profiles
docs.text:
• Cylindrical rotation, constant on cylinders: \(\Delta\Omega = \varepsilon\thinspace r^2\sin^2\theta\), that is \(f_0 = (2/3)\thinspace \varepsilon r^2\) and \(f_2 = -(2/3)\thinspace \varepsilon r^2\). It gives \(\sigma_2 = \sigma_4 = 0\) in both versions, as it must: a barotropic rotation needs no thermal wind.
  • Conical rotation, constant on radial lines: \(\Delta\Omega = \varepsilon\sin^2\theta\). It gives the values below. For \(\varepsilon > 0\) (equator faster, as in the Sun's convection zone) the poles are warmer than the equator, the known solar sense.
\[ \sigma_2 = \frac{16\thinspace \varepsilon r}{21\thinspace \mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g}, \qquad \sigma_4 = -\frac{8\thinspace \varepsilon r}{35\thinspace \mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g}, \qquad S_{tw}(\text{pole}) - S_{tw}(\text{equator}) = \frac{\varepsilon r}{\mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g} > 0 . \]
  • The 'solar' fit, a tanh step at the tachocline radius rtc. Here \(f_0'\) and \(f_2'\) are localised at the tachocline. The \((4/7)\thinspace f_2/r\) and \(-(12/35)\thinspace f_2/r\) parts of (3) fill the convection zone, where kore's \(S_0'\) is zero, so there \(S_{tw}\) is the only background entropy gradient.

docs.title: How large is the thermal wind
docs.text:
Take the solar case: Beyonce = 4.9e4, \(f_2 = -0.198\), \(r \approx 0.9\), \(g \approx 1\). Then \(\sigma_2 \approx 4\times10^{-6}\) and \(\sigma_4 \approx -10^{-6}\). The pole-minus-equator contrast of \(S_{tw}\) is about \(5\times10^{-6}\) in units of \(c_p\) (kore's \(s\) is \(\delta s/c_p\)). With \(c_p \approx 3.5\times10^{8}\) that is \(\approx 1.9\times10^{3}\) erg g⁻¹ K⁻¹, the thermal-wind value at the top of the range Bekki et al. scan.

The small number is misleading. \(S_{tw}\) scales as \(1/(\mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g)\), while the buoyancy it produces is \(\mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g\thinspace s\). So in the convection zone, where \(S_0' = 0\), the entropy perturbation driven by term (c) feeds back on the momentum equation at order \(\Delta\Omega\) relative to the Coriolis force, independently of Beyonce. That is the same order as the momentum diff-rot term. The thermal-wind terms are therefore leading order for convection-zone modes, not a correction: this is the baroclinic coupling that destabilises the high-latitude modes in Bekki et al.

docs.title: Prescribed latitudinal entropy (thermal_wind = 3)
docs.text:
Bekki et al. 2024 (and Bekki et al. 2022, eq. 26) impose a latitudinal entropy gradient that is independent of \(\Omega\) and uniform in \(r\):

\[ \frac{\partial s}{\partial\theta} = \Delta_\theta s\thinspace \sin 2\theta . \]

Since \(\sin 2\theta = -(2/3)\thinspace dP_2/d\theta\), this is \(S_{tw} = \sigma_2 P_2\) with a constant \(\sigma_2\) and nothing else:

\[ \sigma_2 = -\tfrac{2}{3}\thinspace \mathtt{dSdtheta}, \qquad \sigma_4 = \sigma_6 = 0, \qquad \mathtt{dSdtheta} = \Delta_\theta s/c_p . \]

kore's \(s\) is \(\delta s/c_p\), and \(\Delta_\theta s < 0\) gives warm poles. Because \(\sigma_2\) is constant in \(r\), term (b) vanishes and only (c) and (c′) act. \(\Omega\) still enters through (a) and the momentum equation. For uniform rotation use diff_rot_type = 'rigid' with diff_rot_ampl = 0.

docs.title: What is neglected
docs.text:
\(S_{tw}\) is the thermal wind consistent with LBR. The full anelastic balance would add

\[ \frac{S_0'}{\rho_0\thinspace g}\thinspace p_b \]

to \(S_{tw}\). This is the same \(p_1 S_0'\) term that kore drops for the perturbations, so it matters only where \(S_0' \neq 0\) (the radiative zone).

Also neglected, consistently with kore's spherical background, are three effects of relative size \(\Delta\Omega/(\mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g)\) in the anelastic case, negligible for the Sun (Beyonce ≈ 5e4):

  • the perturbation density in the background centrifugal acceleration;
  • the \(\theta\)-dependence of \(\rho_0 T_0\) and \(g\) induced by the thermal wind;
  • the thermal-wind density \(\rho_{tw}\) in the mass flux.

docs.title: 2. The three terms in kore's harmonic form
docs.text: kore expands every field in spherical harmonics of one azimuthal order \(m\) and solves for a radial function per degree \(l\). Multiplying by a function of latitude, such as \(\Delta\Omega\) or \(S_{tw}\), mixes neighbouring degrees. This section writes the three terms as such couplings. All of them are built from two small matrices, \(X\) and \(D\).

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
The entropy and the velocity are

\[ s = \sum_l s_l(r) hinspace S_l^m, \qquad \mathbf u = ho_0^{-1} abla imes abla imes( ho_0 P hinspace \mathbf r) + abla imes(T hinspace \mathbf r), \]

with \(S_l^m\) the Schmidt harmonics of ut.Ylm, \(L = l(l+1)\) and \(h = \ln ho_0\). The terms need two velocity components, for one degree:

\[ u_r = rac{L P}{r} hinspace S_l, \qquad u_ heta = rac{1}{r}\left[\partial_r(rP) + r h' P ight]\partial_ heta S_l + rac{i hinspace m T}{\sin heta} hinspace S_l . \]

docs.title: Angular coupling matrices
docs.text:
With \(x = \cos\theta\), two recurrences define matrices on the degree index at fixed \(m\) (row: target degree \(l'\); column: source degree \(l\)):

\[ \begin{aligned} x\thinspace S_l &= p_l\thinspace S_{l+1} + q_l\thinspace S_{l-1} &&\to X,\cr (1 - x^2)\thinspace \frac{dS_l}{dx} &= (l+1)\thinspace q_l\thinspace S_{l-1} - l\thinspace p_l\thinspace S_{l+1} &&\to D,\cr p_l &= \frac{\sqrt{(l+1)^2 - m^2}}{2l+1}, \qquad q_l = \frac{\sqrt{l^2 - m^2}}{2l+1}. \end{aligned} \]

Multiplying by a polynomial in \(\cos\theta\) is then the same polynomial of the matrix \(X\):

\[ P_2(X) = \frac{3X^2 - 1}{2}, \qquad P_4(X) = \frac{35X^4 - 30X^2 + 3}{8}, \qquad P_2'(X) = 3X, \qquad P_4'(X) = \frac{35X^3 - 15X}{2}. \]

For instance, the non-zero entries of \(P_2(X)\) in column \(l\) are

\[ P_2(X)_ {l,l} = \tfrac12\left[3(p_l\thinspace q_{l+1} + q_l\thinspace p_{l-1}) - 1\right], \qquad P_2(X)_ {l+2,l} = \tfrac32\thinspace p_{l+1}\thinspace p_l, \qquad P_2(X)_ {l-2,l} = \tfrac32\thinspace q_{l-1}\thinspace q_l . \]

In general they are Gaunt coefficients,

\[ X_{l'l} = \sqrt{\frac{2l'+1}{2l+1}}\thinspace \sqrt{\frac{4\pi}{3}}\thinspace (-1)^m\thinspace \mathrm{gaunt}(l',1,l,-m,0,m), \]

and the same with \(n = 2, 4\) in place of 1 for \(P_n(X)\).

docs.title: The terms
docs.text:
Row \(l'\) of the heat equation gains the following terms, before the \(r^2 p_0\) row weight. \(L_l\) is that of the source degree \(l\).

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{(a) advection:}\quad & i\thinspace m G\thinspace \left[f_0\thinspace \delta_{l'l} + f_2\thinspace P_2(X)_ {l'l}\right] s_l ,\cr \text{(b) radial:}\quad & \frac{L_l P_l}{r}\left[\sigma_2'\thinspace P_2(X)_ {l'l} + \sigma_4'\thinspace P_4(X)_ {l'l}\right],\cr \text{(c) latitudinal, from } P\text{:}\quad & \frac{P_l + r P_l' + r h' P_l}{r^2}\left[\sigma_2\thinspace (3XD)_ {l'l} + \sigma_4\left(\tfrac12(35X^3 - 15X)D\right)_ {l'l}\right],\cr \text{(c}'\text{) latitudinal, from } T\text{:}\quad & -\frac{i\thinspace m T_l}{r}\left[\sigma_2\thinspace (3X)_ {l'l} + \sigma_4\left(\tfrac12(35X^3 - 15X)\right)_ {l'l}\right]. \end{aligned} \] term couples \(\Delta l\) (a) advection \(s \to s\) \(0, \pm 2\) (b) radial \(P \to s\) \(0, \pm 2, \pm 4\) (c) latitudinal, \(P\) \(P \to s\) \(0, \pm 2, \pm 4\) (c′) latitudinal, \(T\) \(T \to s\) \(\pm 1, \pm 3\)

Remarks:

  • With thermal_wind = 2 the sums run to \(\sigma_6\), and \(\Delta l\) goes up to \(\pm 6\) for \(P\) and \(\pm 5\) for \(T\). The extra polynomial is given below.
  • The even \(\Delta l\) for \(P\) and odd \(\Delta l\) for \(T\) match the equatorial-symmetry classes of ut.ell (section h uses the poloidal set of degrees). So the block structure is that of the momentum diff-rot blocks, with \(\Delta l = \pm 4\) added.
  • For \(m = 0\) the terms (a) and (c′) vanish. The couplings into \(l = 0\), which is absent from kore's basis, are harmless: nothing feeds back from \(s_0\).
  • Build \(P_2(X)\), \(P_4(X)\) and \(P_n'(X)D\) from \(X\) and \(D\) with about five degrees more than lmax, and cut afterwards. Formed at lmax they are wrong in the top degrees (errors of order one in the entries).
  • Term (a) is anti-Hermitian. In the entropy budget it only shifts the frequency, by an amount set by \(\int p_0\thinspace \Delta\Omega\thinspace \lvert s\rvert^2\thinspace dV\), while (b) and (c) exchange entropy "energy" with the flow.

The polynomial needed for \(\sigma_6\) is

\[ P_6'(X) = \frac{1386X^5 - 1260X^3 + 210X}{16}. \]

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
sympy, 0 failures; tests/heat_dr/tw_sympy.py and heat_check.py repeat the main checks:

  • (3) against direct integration of (2);
  • the curl of the background balance vanishes with \(S_{tw}\) in place (linear and exact);
  • the barotropic check of §1;
  • the matrices \(X\), \(D\), \(P_2(X)\), \(P_4(X)\), \(P'(X)D\) against quadrature projections for \(m = 0\ldots 3\);
  • (b), (c), (c′) against the full 3-D \(\mathbf u\cdot\nabla S_{tw}\) built from \(P\), \(T\) and \(\ln\rho_0\) with sympy and projected on \(S_{l'}\), for \(m = 0, 1, 2\) and every \(\Delta l\).

Independent readers redid the thermal wind with full spherical vector calculus, the linearisation, the couplings with Wigner 3j symbols, and the velocity sign conventions against kore's assembled Coriolis operator. None found a discrepancy.

docs.title: 3. What kore needs
docs.text: This section maps the terms of §2 onto kore's building blocks: radial profiles (functions of \(r\) known on the radial grid), operator labels, and the assembly loops.

docs.title: Radial profiles
docs.text:
• \(f_0\) and \(f_2\) exist already (abu, aub).
  • New are \(\sigma_2\) and \(\sigma_4\) from (3). They need \(g\), \(g'\), \(f'\) and \(f''\): gra, and spv/svp and psl/pls, which give \(r f'\) and \(r^2 f''\).
  • Following pdS = \(p_0\thinspace dS/dr\) and kps = \(\kappa p_0\), the code uses the products tw2 = \(p_0\sigma_2\), tw4 = \(p_0\sigma_4\), tp2 = \(p_0\sigma_2'\) and tp4 = \(p_0\sigma_4'\). Separate tp profiles are needed because a label such as h1tw21_D0 would mean \(r\thinspace (p_0\sigma_2)'\thinspace P\), the derivative of the product, which is not (b).

docs.title: Parity in a full sphere
docs.text: At ricb = 0, \(\sigma_2\) and \(\sigma_4\) are even in \(r\) (\(f\) is even, \(f'\) and \(g\) are odd). So tw2 and tw4 are even, like all other profiles. But tp2 and tp4 are odd. They must be added to the adj lists of submatrices.py (lines 286 and 340; also tests/heat_dr/ebal.py and ru_insane.row_parity), next to gra, pdS and dSd. Otherwise term (b) is silently dropped in full-sphere runs. (The 'solar' profile's parity defect in \(r\) is fixed by evaluating the profiles at \(\lvert r\rvert\), §5.)

docs.title: Operators and labels
docs.text:
Like the other section-h operators, the rows are multiplied by \(r^2 p_0\) and divided by \(L_{l'}^3\):

term operator labels column, \(\Delta l\) (a) \(i\thinspace m\thinspace r^2 p_0 f_0\thinspace s\) and \(i\thinspace m\thinspace r^2 p_0 f_2\thinspace P_2(X)\thinspace s\) h0pss0abu0_D0, h0pss0aub0_D0 \(s\); \(0, \pm 2\) (b) \(L_l\thinspace r\thinspace p_0\thinspace \sigma_n'\thinspace P_n(X)\thinspace P\) h1tp20_D0, h1tp40_D0 \(P\); \(0, \pm 2, \pm 4\) (c) \(p_0\thinspace \sigma_n\left[P + r P' + r h' P\right] P_n'(X)\thinspace D\) h2tw20_D0, h1tw20_D1, h1tw20lho1_D0 (and tw4) \(P\) (c′) \(-i\thinspace m\thinspace r\thinspace p_0\thinspace \sigma_n\thinspace P_n'(X)\thinspace T\) h1tw20_D0, h1tw40_D0 \(T\); \(\pm 1, \pm 3\)

All twelve labels parse with utils.decode_label (the 13-character two-function form for the first and last of (c)).

docs.title: Signs and factors
docs.text:
The section-h rows of \(A\) hold the right-hand side of the heat equation: thermal_advection enters as \(-r p_0 S_0' u_r\), with \(B\) = +entropy. So the three left-hand-side terms of (1) go into \(A\) with a minus sign. This is opposite to the momentum rows, where \(B\) = −inertia and the diff-rot block is added with +.

  • (a) carries the factor Gaspard, like the momentum diff-rot operator. Both had none before the second round, so only timescale = 'rotation' was right.
  • (b), (c) and (c′) carry \(G^2\) through \(\sigma_n\) (but not with thermal_wind = 3).
  • thermal_wind = 0/1/2/3 selects whether (b), (c) and (c′) are included, and in which form; (a) always is.

docs.title: Assembly
docs.text:
• In submatrices.py the \(T\)-column labels are registered with vector parity vT, the others with vP.
  • assemble.py section h used to call only diagonal operators. It needs an \(s\)-column loop over \(\Delta l \in \lbrace -2, 0, 2\rbrace\), a \(P\)-column loop over \(\lbrace -4, \ldots, 4\rbrace\) and a \(T\)-column loop over \(\lbrace -3, -1, 1, 3\rbrace\). These use the offd of operators.differential_rotation: for \(P\) and \(s\), offd = \(\Delta l/2\); for \(T\), the symm-dependent offsets of its 'utor' branches.
  • The thermal boundary rows and forced runs need no change: every 'h' label carries the bc rows, and −i wf entropy is already added.

docs.title: Without thermal diffusion (ThermaD = 0)
docs.text:
With ThermaD = 0 the section-h rows are \(r \times (\mathrm{eq})/p_0\) in a \(C^{(0)}\) basis. Term (a) then becomes h0abu0_D0 and h0aub0_D0 (no \(p_0\)). Terms (b), (c) and (c′) do not fit there: the \(r\) row weight makes the \(P/r\) part of (c) non-polynomial, and the basis has no \(C^{(1)}\) for the \(P'\) term.

So with ThermaD = 0 and thermal_wind ≥ 1 (decided only in utils.adiab_tw), the section-h rows are \(r^2 \times (\mathrm{eq})/p_0\) in a \(C^{(1)}\) basis: gebasis[2] = 1, still no bc rows, chop = 0. The labels are the same (decode_label gives section h the \(r^2\) weight), and tw2/4/6, tp2/4/6 are \(\sigma_n\) and \(\sigma_n'\) without \(p_0\). With ThermaD = 0 and thermal_wind = 0 or diff_rot = 0 nothing changes (\(r \times (\mathrm{eq})/p_0\) in \(C^{(0)}\)). Details and tests are in thermad0.md.

submatrices.py raises an error if a label's derivative order is above its section's basis. Before, G[gbx][gbx-dx] with dx > gbx indexed from the end of the list, which silently picked a wrong basis.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
The new powers couple different \(l\). utils4pp (used by spin_doctor) therefore builds the diff-rot force and heat terms on an \((r, \cos\theta)\) grid once per mode (diff_rot_setup) and projects them back on the harmonics, so that each per-\(l\) worker can pair them with its own \(l\) (§5). The matrix-level budget, heat_blocks() in tests/heat_dr/ebal.py, is the independent check. It verifies the entropy balance

\[ \lambda\langle E\rangle - \langle A\rangle - \langle D\rangle - \langle H\rangle = 0 . \]

docs.title: 4. Benchmarks and which terms they need
docs.text:
Mirouh et al. 2016 (JFM 800, 213; kore shellular_boussinesq). Boussinesq, with the rotation profile imposed from Rieutord 2006's baroclinic flow and a radial \(T_0\) only:

\[ \Omega(r) = 1 + \frac{N^2}{2}\thinspace (1 - r^2). \]

Their heat equation (2.9) is

\[ (\lambda + i\thinspace m\Omega)\thinspace T + r v_r = \frac{E}{P}\thinspace \Delta T . \]

It needs (a) only, with \(S_{tw} = 0\): their background is balanced by centrifugal buoyancy, which kore does not carry. With (3) switched on, \(\sigma_2 = 2N^2r^2/(3\thinspace \mathrm{Beyonce})\) would be as large as \(S_0'\), and the comparison would test the wrong model. kore runs it with structure 'uniform', stratification 'linear' and thermal_wind = 0 (differential_rotation_details.md §11).

Bekki et al. 2022. Fully compressible, solar \(\rho_0\), helioseismic \(\Omega\), and \(S_{tw}\) from (2) with the full \(\Omega^2\), with \(s_0\) uniform in \(r\). It needs (a), (c) and (c′). kore's \(S_{tw}\) also has (b), which they drop by construction. The momentum terms of their eq. (1),

\[ -(\Omega-\Omega_0)\thinspace \partial_\phi\mathbf v - 2\Omega\thinspace \hat{\mathbf z}\times\mathbf v - r\sin\theta\thinspace (\mathbf v\cdot\nabla\Omega), \]

are kore's existing diff-rot operator.

Baruteau & Rieutord 2013, Guenel et al. 2016, Astoul et al. 2021. thermal = 0, so unaffected.

docs.title: 6. Benchmark: solar inertial modes (Bekki et al. 2022, Mukhopadhyay et al. 2025)
docs.text:
The best target is Mukhopadhyay, Bekki, Zhu & Gizon 2025 (A&A, arXiv 2501.16797). It uses the set-up of Bekki, Cameron & Gizon 2022 with Model S, and tabulates modes to 1e-4 nHz for compressible, anelastic and Boussinesq models. Their anelastic model is kore's.

The set-up is that of tests/diff_rot/mk_bekki.py with drtype=Y20: N 64, lmax \(m + 63\), \(\nu = \kappa = 10^{12}\) cm² s⁻¹, \(\delta = 0\) (adiabatic background, \(S_0' = 0\)). This section uses kore's \(P_0 + P_2\) rotation profile; §8 repeats the comparison with their full \(\Omega(r, \theta)\).

Uniform rotation. kore matches their anelastic Tables C.1–C.4 to 0.006 nHz or better for 27 modes (\(n = 0\) and 1 Rossby, high-frequency retrograde (HFR), columnar; \(m = 1\ldots 16\)). This needs the Model S density: the stock 'smoothed sun' fit is up to 48 % off near the surface, which moves the \(n = 1\), HFR and columnar modes by 1.5–8 nHz (18 at \(m = 16\)).

Time unit (Gaspard). The same problem solved with time unit \(1/\Omega_0\) (\(G = 1\)) and with time unit \(1/\Omega_{\rm Carrington}\) (\(G \neq 1\)), in the same frame, agrees to 2e-6 nHz.

Frame. Changing the frame itself (426.86 vs 456 nHz, with \(\Delta\Omega\) redefined relative to it) does not matter with thermal_wind = 2 (2e-6 nHz); with thermal_wind = 1 it moves modes by 0.1–0.9 nHz.

Differential rotation (their Tables C.5–C.9, thermal_wind = 2 without \(u_r\thinspace \partial_r S_{tw}\), as in the papers). kore minus target, in nHz:

  • \(n = 0\) Rossby: within 0.8;
  • \(n = 1\) Rossby: within 1.1–2.7;
  • high-latitude, m 1 and 2: within 0.2–1.5;
  • HFR: 2.7–6.2;
  • columnar: 3.4–9.2, growing with \(m\).

The remaining difference is the rotation profile. kore's \(\Omega\) here has \(P_0 + P_2\) only (4.5 nHz too fast at the equator, 12 at the pole); theirs has \(P_4\) and radial shear.

Term (b). Keeping \(u_r\thinspace \partial_r S_{tw}\) (kore always did before §8 added the switch) moves columnar modes by 5–15 nHz and HFR modes by 8–10 nHz. At \(\delta = 0\) it also makes the low latitudes superadiabatic: \(m = 1\) symm +1 then has a weakly growing mode (12.4 nHz, growth 1.8 nHz).

Not reproduced with the \(P_0 + P_2\) profile:

  • the growing \(m = 1\) high-latitude mode of Bekki et al. 2022 (−90.9 nHz, growth 14.1 nHz); kore's nearest modes are damped by 3 nHz;
  • the baroclinic onset of Bekki et al. 2024; kore needs a 4–8 times larger \(\Delta_\theta s\).

Both were caused by the \(P_2\)-only rotation profile. With the observed \(\Omega(r, \theta)\), kore has the growing high-latitude mode (+11.3 nHz; Mukhopadhyay et al. 2025: +11.7) and the onset near 500 (§8).

The \(\Delta_\theta s\) runs used a run-local edit of \(\sigma_2\), \(\sigma_4\). With thermal_wind = 3 and dSdtheta = \(\Delta_\theta s/c_p\), the warm-poles case at 4000 erg g⁻¹ K⁻¹ gives \(A\) and \(B\) bitwise equal to that run (−101.42 nHz, growth +7.30 nHz).

docs.title: 7. Still open
docs.text:
• Done in §8: the switch thermal_wind_radial for \(u_r\thinspace \partial_r S_{tw}\) (term (b)), \(P_4\) ('solar_P4') and tabulated \(\Omega(r, \theta)\), the Model S density (now structure 'old model S prototype'), and the amplitude controls.
  • ThermaD = 0 with thermal_wind ≥ 1 is implemented (\(r^2\) rows in \(C^{(1)}\), §3) and tested (thermad0.md). Open there:
    • the ThermaD → 0 limit with fixed-entropy walls has an unresolved boundary layer;
    • without diffusion the thermal wind has small-scale growing modes that are not converged in lmax;
    • its rows carry \(\sigma_n\thinspace (\ln\rho)'\) (term (c)) without \(p_0\), which converges slowly in N when \(\rho\) nearly vanishes at the surface (structure 'Wu 2005' with r_out → 1, ricb = 0). The \(p_0\)-weighted checks do not see it; tests/heat_dr/row_check.py does.
  • The density of the 8-term fit near the surface (§6): structure 'model S hydrostatic' (§8) avoids it, and new runs use it.
  • 'Y20-wall-bounded' and 'shellular' (except even \(\sigma > 0\)) at ricb = 0 are not smooth at \(r = 0\); this is now a WARNING.
  • The Boussinesq background (now structure 'uniform') runs with the differential rotation since 2026-10-23, when the rotation profiles stopped depending on the background model (differential_rotation_details.md §11). The models read from a file ('poly', 'mesa', 'gsm', 'astropy table') never ran on this branch and were removed on 2026-10-26.
  • tests/heat_dr/csolve.py has no equilibration (kore's solve.py has Ruiz scaling); it now warns when every eigenvalue comes back equal to the shift.

docs.title: 8. Generic differential rotation: any Pₙ, 'solar_P4', 'tabulated' (2026-10-13)
docs.text:
Commit 92a0d020. The rotation profile is no longer limited to \(P_0 + P_2\). It can be any sum of even Legendre polynomials, each with an amplitude factor \(a_n\):

\[ \Delta\Omega = \sum_{n\ \text{even}} a_n\thinspace f_n(r)\thinspace P_n(\cos\theta). \]

This makes the observed solar rotation usable, either as a fit ('solar_P4') or as a helioseismic table ('tabulated').

docs.title: Momentum couplings
docs.text:
\(n = 0\) and 2 keep the closed forms of diff_rot_coefficients.py. For \(n \ge 4\) the new bin/diff_rot_generic.py projects the diff-rot force of each source degree on the target degrees:

\[ \mathbf W = G\left[\Delta\Omega\thinspace (i\thinspace m\thinspace \mathbf u + 2\hat{\mathbf z}\times\mathbf u) + \sin\theta\thinspace \left(r\thinspace \partial_r\Delta\Omega\thinspace u_r + \partial_\theta\Delta\Omega\thinspace u_\theta\right)\hat{\mathbf e}_ \phi\right]. \]
  • The projection uses Gauss–Legendre quadrature in \(\cos\theta\), exact for these polynomial integrands.
  • It turns the 12 primitive projections into the 18 coefficients of the existing labels, in the naming and normalisation of diff_rot_coefficients.py. They are cached per \((n, m)\) and built to \(\mathrm{lmax} + n + 6\).
  • The radial profiles \(f_n\), \(r f_n'\) and \(r^2 f_n''\) have the codes abN, svN, plN (N = 4, 6, 8, then a, c, e, g for 10–16).
  • Couplings: \(P \to P\) and \(T \to T\) have \(\lvert\Delta l\rvert \le n\), and \(P \leftrightarrow T\) have \(\lvert\Delta l\rvert \le n + 1\), so assemble.py loops over \(\Delta l\) up to utils.dr_nmax (+1).
  • diff_rot_generic = 1 builds \(n = 0, 2\) with the quadrature too, as a self-check (agrees to ~1e-12).

docs.title: Thermal-wind entropy
docs.text:
For thermal_wind = 1 or 2 with degrees above 2, radial_profiles.sigma_all computes the Legendre coefficients of

\[ \frac{\partial S}{\partial x} = -\frac{r^2G^2}{\mathrm{Beyonce}\thinspace g}\left[x\thinspace \partial_r F + \frac{(1 - x^2)\thinspace \partial_x F}{r}\right], \qquad F = 2\Delta\Omega \ \ \text{or}\ \ (1 + \Delta\Omega)^2 - 1, \]

by quadrature on the Chebyshev nodes, and integrates in \(x\). \(\sigma_n'\) comes from Chebyshev differentiation.

  • \(S_{tw}\) has degrees \(2\ldots\mathrm{nmax} + 2\) (thermal_wind 1) or \(2\ldots 2\thinspace \mathrm{nmax} + 2\) (thermal_wind 2).
  • Profiles: tw2…tw8, twa, twc, …, twy (\(n = 34\)) for \(\sigma_n\), and tp* for \(\sigma_n'\).
  • heat_dr_coefficients.py builds \(P_n(X)\), \(P_n'(X)\) and \(P_n'(X)D\) for any \(n\) by the Legendre recurrence.
  • thermal_wind = 3 is unchanged (\(\sigma_2\) only).

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
'solar_P4' is an analytic fit with \(P_0\), \(P_2\) and \(P_4\), with an erf step at the tachocline:

\[ \Omega = \Omega_{\rm RZ} + \left[\Omega_{\rm CZ}(\theta) - \Omega_{\rm RZ}\right]\frac{1 + \mathrm{erf}\big((x - \mathrm{rtc})/\mathrm{dtc}\big)}{2}, \qquad \Omega_{\rm CZ} = c_0 + c_2\cos^2\theta + c_4\cos^4\theta . \]

diff_rot_solar = [\(c_0\), \(c_2\), \(c_4\), \(\Omega_{\rm RZ}\), rtc, dtc] = [464, −76, −50, 433.5, 0.71, 0.045] (nHz and \(R_\odot\); Mukhopadhyay et al. 2026).

'tabulated' reads \(\Omega(r, \theta)\) from diff_rot_file, an .npz with ome[θ, r] (nHz), r (R☉) and theta (rad). This is the layout of the Mukhopadhyay et al. 2025 Edmond file data/diff_rot.npz; tests/diff_rot/ls_to_edmond_layout.py converts the Larson & Schou 2018 table. At each table radius the profile is projected on \(P_0\ldots P_{\mathrm{nmax}}\) (diff_rot_nmax, 4–16), then fitted over the shell by a Chebyshev series of degree diff_rot_rdeg (24). The fit and truncation errors are printed.

Both use \(\Delta\Omega = \Omega/\Omega_{\rm ref} - 1\), with \(\Omega_{\rm ref}/2\pi\) = diff_rot_frame (456 nHz), and \(x = r\cdot\)r_out for a solar structure. For the Edmond profile the truncation error at nmax 8 is up to 17 nHz near the poles at the surface; nmax 12 is the working choice.

docs.title: Amplitude controls
docs.text:
These apply to every profile type:

  • diff_rot_term_amp = \([a_0, a_2, \ldots, a_{16}]\) multiplies each \(P_n\) term of \(\Delta\Omega\) (missing entries are 1).
  • diff_rot_ampl multiplies the whole of \(\Delta\Omega\), for every type. (Until 2026-10-23 it was diff_rot_amplitude, which was the exponent of 'shellular' and \(N_0^2\) of 'shellular_boussinesq'.)
  • thermal_wind_amplitude multiplies \(S_{tw}\), which is otherwise the thermal wind of the scaled \(\Delta\Omega\).
  • thermal_wind_radial = 0 drops \(u_r\thinspace \partial_r S_{tw}\) (term (b)), as the papers do; 1 (default) keeps it.

docs.title: Model S density
docs.text:
This is a legacy structure, kept so that older runs reproduce; new runs use the hydrostatic structure below. structure = 'old model S prototype' (formerly solar_density = 'model S') replaces the \(\ln\rho\) and \(\ln p\) of the 8-term fit by Chebyshev fits of bin/model_s.at; \(g\) stays the 8-term one, so the three are not in hydrostatic balance. The fit has degree solar_density_deg (30) on solar_density_window, by default the shell widened by 0.01 below and 0.005 above. It reproduces the run-local Model S fit of the §6 benchmark runs: \(A\) and \(B\) are bitwise equal.

The shell fit is not even in \(r\), so it cannot be used with ricb = 0. solar_density_window = 'sun' (the default when ricb = 0) fits Model S once over the whole Sun instead: the table is mirrored to \(x < 0\), fitted on \([-W, W]\), \(W\) = r_out + 0.005, with degree solar_density_sun_deg (60), and the odd coefficients are dropped, so \(\ln\rho\) and \(\ln p\) are even and smooth at \(r = 0\). The fit is the same for every ricb. Its error is \(1.7\times10^{-3}\) in \(\ln\rho\) and \(2.6\times10^{-4}\) in \(\ln p\), mostly at 0.70–0.72 R☉, where Model S has a sharp feature at the base of the convection zone (the shell fit reaches \(2\times10^{-4}\) there). On the §8 shell it moves the m 3 Rossby n0 and n1 modes by ≤ 0.001 nHz.

docs.title: Hydrostatic structure
docs.text:
structure = 'model S hydrostatic' fits only \(\ln\rho\) and derives the rest, so the background is in hydrostatic balance. \(\ln\rho\) is one even polynomial of degree structure_deg (30) over the whole Sun, fitted to bin/model_s.at on \(0 \le x \le\) r_out (iteratively reweighted least squares, close to minimax in \(\ln\rho\)). Then, with \(\rho\) in units of \(\rho_c\),

\[m(x) = \int_0^x \rho\, x'^2\, dx', \qquad g = \frac{m(x)}{x^2\, m(1)}, \qquad \frac{dp}{dx} = -K \rho\, g,\]

\(g\) normalised at the surface as the 8-term fit (\(m(1)\) takes Model S above r_out), \(K\) the Model S value of \(-p'/(\rho g)\), and \(p\) integrated inward from Model S at r_out. \(\rho\) and \(p\) are normalised at the centre.

structure_deg 24 30 40 50 60 largest error in \(\rho\), \(p\), \(g\) (%) 2.4, 1.4, 1.9 1.0, 0.5, 0.75 0.33, 0.14, 0.24 0.14, 0.06, 0.10 0.10, 0.03, 0.08 full-sphere HFR m 8, \(\omega\) \(\sigma\) (nHz) −237.49 −32.49 −236.75 −33.69 −236.79 −34.91 −236.59 −34.61 −236.60 −34.57

The errors are the largest against Model S on \(0 \le x \le 0.985\); the HFR m 8 values are for examples/smooth_sun/parameters.py as it was on 2026-10-24, with \(\delta_{cz} = 0\) and diff_rot_hold = 0.6 (without the hold, degree 30 gives −236.73 −33.44). The mode stops changing at degree 50 (0.05 nHz to 60), and HL1 at degree 40. Degree 30 runs at the resolution of degree 24 (N 640, lmax 79 for HFR m 8); degrees of 40 and above need about 16 more lmax for ℓ-convergence below \(10^{-4}\). Use 50 to match papers that use Model S itself: at degree 40 already, Mukhopadhyay et al. 2025b's HFR m 7 comes out within 0.03 nHz in \(\omega\) and 0.12 nHz in \(\sigma\) of the old prototype's fit, against 1.0 and 0.6 nHz at degree 24. This is the structure for new runs, full sphere or shell. The other two, '8-term fit' and 'old model S prototype', are legacy, kept so that older runs reproduce.

With stratification 'solar_rz' a convection-zone superadiabaticity \(\delta\) (Bekki 2024, eq. 2) can be added to \(dS/dr\):

\[\frac{dS}{dr} \mathrel{+}= \delta(x)\,\frac{d\ln p}{dr}\,\frac{1 + \mathrm{erf}((|x| - x_{OS})/d_{OS})}{2}, \qquad \delta(x) = \delta_{cz} + (\delta_{sf} - \delta_{cz})\, e^{-((|x| - 0.985)/0.015)^2},\]

with \(\delta_{cz}\), \(\delta_{sf}\) = solar_rz_delta_cz, solar_rz_delta_sf (0: no term) and \(\delta < 0\) subadiabatic.

Fitted to the HFR frequencies \(\omega\) of Hanson et al. (2022) with structure = 'model S hydrostatic' (degrees 24, 30 and 50 give the same), thermal_wind = 2, thermal_wind_radial = 0 and \(\delta_{sf} = 0\): the MCA frequencies of \(m\) = 4, 8, 12, 14 give \(\delta_{cz} = -2.1\times10^{-7}\) (\(1\sigma\): \(-2.6\) to \(-1.6\times10^{-7}\), RMS 6.8 nHz); the RDA frequencies of \(m\) = 8, 9, 12, 13, 14 give \(-3.7\times10^{-7}\) (RMS 19 nHz, \(m\) = 8 and 9 still 25 to 33 nHz too prograde), and both together \(-2.9\times10^{-7}\). These fits were made with diff_rot_hold = 0.6.

examples/smooth_sun uses \(-4\times10^{-7}\), without diff_rot_hold. Its HFR \(m = 8\) is then at \(\omega = -271.19\), \(\sigma = -33.18\) nHz, 34.46 nHz more retrograde than at \(\delta_{cz} = 0\) (\(-236.73\), \(-33.44\)). At the MCA value, \(-2.1\times10^{-7}\), the \(m = 8\) HFR mode mixes with deep-core r modes (\(\ell = 9\), near 0.14 R☉) once the hold is gone.
